items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: The interviewee addresses the interviewer as 'Tom' multiple times (e.g., 'Well, I'll tell you, Tom.'), indicating Tom is the interviewer, not a subject of a professional or personal relationship within the jazz context described.

ctx.x: Let me ask you about playing with the George Lewis band and what sort of a band you thought it was and how you played and how you particularly yourself played.

Well, I'll tell you, Tom. George Lewis wanted the best or nothing at all. And he did get that recognition for his rhythm section. He was supposed to have the best rhythm section on it. That was including Elton Pennell, Slow Drag, Lawrence, and myself. And when he got that, he was satisfied. But, he wants you to keep that drive. See, that was a driving beat that he had me working on. That wasn't exactly what you would call an authentic jazz beat. See? Because if you listen plainly to Saeed, you don't hear that…
Did George give you any particular instructions as to how he wanted you to play?
